performance_tasks.brief:
(1) Why is a sawn timber plank still classed as a natural material?
A. Cutting makes a natural polymer synthetic
B. Sawing reshapes the existing natural material
C. A shaped object must be chemically synthesised
D. Natural classification depends on its original shape [1]

(2) Which statement explains a useful property and a limitation of window glass?
A. Transmits light and bends without breaking
B. Resists impact but blocks visible light
C. Bends readily but scratches very easily
D. Transmits light but fractures under impact [1]

(3) Why is concrete not the same material as cement?
A. Concrete is cement with no aggregate added
B. Concrete and cement differ only in drying time
C. Concrete includes cement binder and aggregate
D. Concrete is cement before it reacts with water [1]

(4) Why can a nylon strand be described both as a fibre and as a synthetic polymer?
A. Both terms describe only the strand’s origin
B. Fibre describes composition while polymer describes shape
C. They describe different aspects of nylon
D. Synthetic describes a material found in organisms [1]

(5) Why can concrete contain both ionic and covalent bonding?
A. Constituents have different chemical structures
B. Constituents must have identical bonding
C. Mixing changes all bonds to covalent
D. Water makes all constituents ionic [1]

(6) Which statement correctly relates cellulose and its origin?
A. It is synthetic because it has long chains
B. It is a natural polymer with covalent bonds
C. It is a natural mixture of small molecules
D. It is a natural polymer with ionic chains [1]

(7) Which building-material choice is linked to an appropriate property?
A. Glass windows: transmission of visible light
B. Copper cable coverings: high electrical conductivity
C. Glass bending brackets: resistance to scratching
D. Concrete flexible sheets: high compressive strength [1]

(8) Why does concrete harden after water is added to cement and aggregate?
A. Only evaporation of added water causes setting
B. Water dissolves aggregate into one homogeneous solid
C. Hydration of cement binds the aggregate
D. Cooling rather than hydration binds the ingredients [1]

(9) Which arrangement helps disperse a grease droplet in water?
A. Heads in grease, tails facing water
B. Heads and tails both inside grease
C. Heads and tails both outside grease
D. Tails in grease, heads facing water [1]

(10) Which statement correctly describes soap preparation from oil?
A. Acid neutralisation alone converts oil to soap
B. Mixing with cold water completes the reaction
C. Heating oil alone gives soap without an alkali
D. Alkaline hydrolysis produces soap and glycerol [1]

(11) Why can soap clean less efficiently in hard water?
A. Hard-water ions keep more soap dissolved
B. Insoluble scum consumes some of the soap
C. Hardness prevents any soap from forming lather
D. The soap neutralises all the water molecules [1]

(12) Which approximate dimensional range is used for nanomaterials here?
A. 1–100 nm
B. 1–100 mm
C. 1–100 cm
D. 1–100 m [1]
marking_guidance_must_name: Part 1: Correct option B (1). B. Sawing reshapes the existing natural material. Mechanical shaping does not change the natural origin of the wood. Distractor explanations: A: Cutting changes shape without synthesising new polymer chains. C: Shaping does not imply chemical synthesis. D: Natural origin is not lost when the material is reshaped. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 2: Correct option D (1). D. Transmits light but fractures under impact. Transparency suits windows; brittleness limits impact resistance. Distractor explanations: A: Ordinary window glass is brittle rather than readily bendable. B: Window glass transmits light and is vulnerable to impact. C: Glass is not readily flexible; this combination misstates its behaviour. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 3: Correct option C (1). C. Concrete includes cement binder and aggregate. Cement is one ingredient of the concrete mixture. Distractor explanations: A: Concrete contains aggregate as well as cement. B: Their composition differs, not merely drying time. D: Concrete is a mixture including aggregate, not an earlier stage of cement. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 4: Correct option C (1). C. They describe different aspects of nylon. Classification can use different criteria. Distractor explanations: A: Fibre describes form; polymer describes molecular structure, not just origin. B: This reverses the roles of fibre and polymer. D: Synthetic means manufactured by chemical synthesis, not produced by organisms. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 5: Correct option A (1). A. Constituents have different chemical structures. Concrete is a mixture, so its constituents need not share one bonding type. Distractor explanations: B: A mixture can retain constituents with different bonding types. C: Mixing does not convert all existing bonds into covalent bonds. D: Adding water does not make every constituent ionic. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 6: Correct option B (1). B. It is a natural polymer with covalent bonds. Natural origin is compatible with a covalent polymer structure. Distractor explanations: A: Long chains establish polymer structure, not synthetic origin. C: Cellulose consists of macromolecular chains, not a mixture of small molecules. D: The bonds within cellulose chains are covalent, not ionic. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 7: Correct option A (1). A. Glass windows: transmission of visible light. Glass transmits light. Distractor explanations: B: A cable covering must insulate; conducting copper would not do so. C: Scratch resistance does not overcome glass brittleness in a bending bracket. D: Compressive strength does not make concrete flexible in thin sheets. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 8: Correct option C (1). C. Hydration of cement binds the aggregate. Hydration produces the hardened binder. Distractor explanations: A: Setting involves chemical hydration, not only loss of water. B: Aggregate is not dissolved into one homogeneous solid. D: Hydration reactions, rather than cooling, create the binding material. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 9: Correct option D (1). D. Tails in grease, heads facing water. The different molecular regions interact with grease and water respectively. Distractor explanations: A: This reverses the hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails. B: Heads need contact with water to stabilise the dispersed droplet. C: Tails must interact with grease rather than both ends remaining in water. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 10: Correct option D (1). D. Alkaline hydrolysis produces soap and glycerol. Hydrolysis changes the fat or oil chemically. Distractor explanations: A: Oil must undergo alkaline hydrolysis; acid neutralisation alone does not make soap. B: Cold water alone does not hydrolyse the oil to soap. C: Alkali is required for the specified soap-making reaction. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 11: Correct option B (1). B. Insoluble scum consumes some of the soap. Calcium/magnesium ions form insoluble soap salts. Distractor explanations: A: Calcium and magnesium ions precipitate soap rather than keep it dissolved. C: Scum wastes soap, but sufficient extra soap can eventually form lather. D: Soap does not neutralise all water molecules; it reacts with hardness ions. No mark for more than one selected option.

Part 12: Correct option A (1). A. 1–100 nm. The nanoscale range is approximately 1–100 nanometres in at least one dimension. Distractor explanations: B: Millimetres are a million times larger than nanometres. C: Centimetres are ten million times larger than nanometres. D: Metres are a billion times larger than nanometres. No mark for more than one selected option.
